_comment: THE TOOL IMPLEMENTATION LAYER of the harness, created 2026-10-01 for bean w2gr. The owner's rulings: (2026-09-30, option A) tool DEFINITIONS stay in cat-harness (cat-harness/tools/ and its discover.ts reader) and this instance IMPLEMENTS them -- the split bootstrap / bootstrap-tools already uses; (2026-10-01) the content core does NOT depend on this instance, so the document adapter was cut into a server-free content class and a server wrapper -- SUPERSEDED the same day by ruling C1, which put this layer BELOW the content core (see `_needs_comment`): the core may depend on it, it may not depend on the core, and a server part that needs the core moves up into it; (2026-10-01) it carries its OWN package.json, like bootstrap-tools; and a content package's own server half lives in a named subgraph of that package rather than here. Step 3a moves the standalone MCP server (adapters/mcp-server/) in and nothing else, so this declaration names only what exists (bean dh4f). The layout MIRRORS cat-harness's (adapters/, src/, test/) so that, as step 3b moves src/ here, the relative imports between modules that move together come out unchanged.

title: C@T Harness Tools
description: What implements the harness's Tool definitions: the MCP servers, their tool registrars and routes. Definitions stay in cat-harness; this layer runs them.

_avatar_comment: A wrench — what implements the harness's tool definitions. Moved here from cat-harness/schemas/content/avatars.ts, 2026-10-05 (bean sod4 #4): an instance declares its own mark.

directories.description: The standalone MCP server (`adapters/mcp-server/`): its tool registrars, the declared tool groups that load them, and the Dockerfile that packages it. Tool implementations live here; their definitions stay in cat-harness.

The validators this layer's code provides, one folio-validator/v1 node each naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks, as cat-harness and the layers above it declare theirs. Among them, `dynamic-state.json` checks the `cat-harness-dynamic-state/v1` document `writeDynamicState` writes; its family is listed in the docs typology here, so its node is here too.

The standalone tool pages the MCP server serves at `/ui/` (`adapters/mcp-server/server.ts`): the bibliography QA, glossary curator and source-relevance pages, their index and shared stylesheet. Static HTML with no build step.

The content viewer the MCP server serves at `/viewer/` (`adapters/mcp-server/server.ts`, `VIEWER_DIR`): one HTML page carrying the whole single-page app, which reads `/api/folio` and opens the first paper the folio lists. A platform viewer, not folio content: it names no folio, and `test/tools/test-server.e2e.ts` and `scripts/tests/ui/viewer-script.test.ts` assert it.

The harness's Zod schema corpus and the tests that exercise it, so this directory is typed `schemas` as well as `code`. cat-harness keeps the schemas that are data: the per-skill JSON Schemas in `schemas/skills/`, `staging-comparison.schema.json` and the PlantUML model.

Scripts this layer runs. `lib/roots.ts` is the one place that names the three roots a file can mean (HARNESS_ROOT, TOOLS_ROOT, REPO_ROOT). `gen-id-lookup.ts` builds the prefix-sharded lookup over a catalogue's REFERENCED nodes for every instance that declares an `id-lookup` directory, and writes it THERE (`bun run cat id-lookup`, gated by `id-lookup:check`); `bench-id-lookup.ts` measures it at full catalogue scale on a seeded synthetic corpus. Neither names a corpus: both read the checkout's declarations. `extract-assets.ts` is the tool behind the harness's `asset-extraction` skill: it turns a container's INDEX into a `folio-extraction/v1` record, whose contract is `schemas/content/extraction.ts`.

The identifier-lookup CLIENT a reader's browser runs: `lookup.js` (plain ES module, no dependencies) with its hand-written `lookup.d.ts`, and a one-form `index.html` told which index to open by `?index=<directory>`. The indexes themselves are generated output hosted by the instance each is about (its own `id-lookup/`), never here. JavaScript, so it never sits under the plain docs pipeline.
Tests of the code this layer holds, among them `composition-roots` (the declared tool groups and route mounting) and `mcp-graph-tools`.

The MCP and HTTP server — what `bun run cat start` and `.mcp.json` start, from `src/index.ts`: the composition roots (`server.ts`, `route-groups.ts`, `tool-groups.ts`), the plug-in contract `types.ts`, the MCP tool registrars (`tools/`), the harness's own routes (`routes/`), authentication (`auth/`, `core/github-auth.ts`), access control (`core/rbac.ts`), the MCP projection (`mcp/`) and the no-content adapter. The Tool nodes it serves are declared in `cat-harness/tools/` with their `src/tools/*` paths, and the loader finds each module here through `needs`. Content routes (feedback, glossary, relevance) live in the content layer that owns their content, and the route loader finds them the same way.

Ambient type declarations for untyped dependencies: `bpmn-moddle.d.ts` and `dmn-moddle.d.ts`. This layer's `tsconfig.json` includes `types/**/*.d.ts`, and so does the content core's (`../cat-harness-tools/types/**/*.d.ts`), so the path is a contract with a layer above and must not move.

`discover.ts`, the reader that finds every declared `tools` graph's Tool nodes by asking the declarations, and `index.ts`, this layer's own `tools` graph: the Tool nodes whose in-process module is code here (`bpmn-engine`), declared beside that code so the module path is instance-relative. Every other Tool node, the shell-invoked ones included, is declared in `cat-harness/tools/`. Declared as a named `code` subgraph, so a remote mount lays it down (the content core's `glossary-extract.ts` imports it) and it is exported by package name (`scripts/package-exports.ts`).

The Python toolchain's dependency manifests: `requirements.txt` (the LEAN set CI installs, `pip install -r cat-harness-tools/python/requirements.txt` from the checkout root) and `requirements-extended.txt` (declared, deliberately not installed in CI — its cost is stated per entry). GENERATED, never hand-edited: the source is `schemas/sdlc/python-deps.ts`, whose `requirementsPath` is the one place this location is written, and `bun run cat deps:python` writes both (`deps:python:check` fails when either is stale). Dependabot's pip `directory:` names this directory. `code`: a dependency manifest is the toolchain's, the same class as a `package.json`.

exempt.visualiser: Owner, 2026-10-29 (cat-harness#691): no viewer by design. Each node is an outside package whose registry tarball and SPDX licence the node already links, so a viewer would only repeat the registry.

directories.title: Software libraries
directories.description: The outside libraries this layer's code imports: one `software-library/1.0.0` node per dependency in `package.json`, with the version and sha512 that `bun.lock` pins, the registry tarball, the SPDX licence read from the installed package, the range, whether it is a dev dependency, the files that import it (`usedBy`) and the `types/*.d.ts` shim that types it (bpmn-moddle, dmn-moddle). GENERATED, never hand-edited: `bun run cat libraries:derive` writes it and `libraries:check` fails on a stale node, an import no node names, and a shim no node names. The kind is cat-harness's; this layer keeps its own nodes because it pins its own versions. `held/<layer>/` holds the nodes of each layer below the kind, which may not name it (bootstrap-tools): `software-library/1.2.0` with `layer` naming the layer it describes, derived at this layer's pins.

directories.title: CI caches
directories.description: The CI caches this layer declares (cache-first CI, rule 6): one `cache/1.0.0` node per cache in this layer's reusable workflows and scripts (`layer-pr-checks.yml`, `pr-tests.yml`), with its key recipe, trust class, location, producer, consumers, save policy, verify and uses; and `cache-inventory/1.0.0` snapshots of the caches found across the harness repositories, dated, which are never read as declarations. `viewer.md` is generated by `bun run cat caches:viz` and held current by `caches:viz:check`; it computes the key today's pins imply and joins the stored key, size and hit rate from the daily cache report, so staleness is computed, never claimed.
The work plan for cat-harness-tools.

The content pipeline — build, render, QA checkers and generators over a folio's content graph. Its QA script sidecars stay in the harness, under `test/results/script-sidecars/`, because they are the harness's QA state.

Files `folio_init` WRITES INTO a new folio, kept as real files rather than strings inside `scripts/init-folio.ts`. `init-folio.ts` looks the directory up by this id (`TEMPLATES_ID`), so the id must not change.

How a folio-assistant host is stood up and kept current: `provision.sh`, `deploy.sh`, `self-update.sh`, `docker-compose.yml`, `Caddyfile.template` and `GOOGLE_OAUTH_SETUP.md`. Its governing skill is `deployment-auth`, whose architecture diagram is of these files.

This layer's pinned-upstream registry, `upstream-pins.json` (`"$schema": "folio-upstream-pins/v1"`): one row for each upstream dependency whose pin literal is in a file this layer holds (today only the pdf.js viewer, pinned in `scripts/pdf-viewer.ts`). Each row names the file the pin is READ from (`pinnedIn`, resolved against this instance's root), the pattern that reads it, and what of ours binds to the dependency; it holds no version. `bun run cat check:upstream-pins` reads it together with cat-harness's `upstream/` registry (`cat-harness-upstream`), which keeps the rows whose files are in the harness, since a harness row naming a file in this layer would be a wrong-direction reference. `code`: the checker's input table, not content any reader renders.
The ArchiMate subgraph's generators, checker and tests. Its Zod schema is in `archimate/schemas/`; its content stays in `cat-harness/archimate/`.
The ArchiMate subgraph's Zod schema. The subgraph's content stays in `cat-harness/archimate/`.
The OpenAPI subgraph's ingester, page generator and tests. Its Zod schema is in `openapi/schemas/`; its content stays in `cat-harness/openapi/`.
The OpenAPI subgraph's Zod schema. The subgraph's content stays in `cat-harness/openapi/`.

Repository health reports for THIS repository: the one `health-report/v1` document `bun run cat-harness-tools/test/health/run.ts --instance <this instance>` writes. Each repository carries its own report. The graph typology is cat-harness's; its `health` entry says what separates a health report (about the repository) from a `qa` verdict (about an artefact). It sits at the root, not under `test/`, because `test/` is declared as code and a declared directory may not nest inside another; at the root a state graph's path equals its id, as `beans/` does.

_needs_comment: The layers this instance sits on: cat-harness, whose Tool DEFINITIONS it implements, and bootstrap-tools, the tool layer one level down. Owner ruling C1 (2026-10-01, epic 7x5n, bean rmi6): this layer sits BELOW the content core -- the order is bootstrap, bootstrap-tools, cat-harness, this layer, then the content layers. It declared the content core as its one need until then, for the document adapter's server wrapper; the placement audit measured 0 of this layer's 27 files importing the core, so the edge was declared and never used. The core now needs THIS layer, and the reverse edge -- anything here importing a layer above -- is wrong-direction, which `check:import-direction` enforces from the declared `needs` lists rather than from any table. The layer above is deliberately not named here: a lower layer naming a higher one is the wrong direction `check:reference-direction` grades.
_gateExemptions_comment: Checks this instance declares and runs in its OWN CI, not in an index's workflows. Read by scripts/gates.ts (bean 0r7u), so an index checkout does not report them as unrun.

scripts.reason: this layer's own CI runs it: `layer-pr-checks.yml` runs every `*:check` script of the calling instance on every pull request, and an index mounts this layer at a pin that has passed it. The committed `caches/viewer.md` is rendered with the layer as root and no cache report, so the check is a byte comparison that does not depend on the checkout.

_canonicalUrl_comment: A placeholder base under this repository's own publication root, not a FHIR canonical. It exists because a Tool node's I/O type IRIs are minted against it at load and Zod refuses a relative one.
_name_comment: THE NAME IS NOT AN INSTANTIATION CLAIM. Instantiation is a `<name>.config.json` at the repository root (`harness-tiles`, bean `6n23`), and there is none for this layer. Staged as a sibling directory like bootstrap-tools; after the split it becomes its own repository and only `livesAt` changes.
